formalDefinition: Sub Cover = {<S,T,k> | S is a set of elements, and there exists a grouping of k T subsetse equal to S}
problemDefinition: Given a set of elements and a collection S of m sets whose union equals the universe, the set cover problem is to identify the smallest sub-collection of S whose union equals the universe
inputDescription: U, a universe of elements, S, a collection of subsets of U, and k, the maximum number of subsets
outputDescription: True or False, whether k subsets from S can be chosen whose union covers U
source: Karp, Richard M. Reducibility among combinatorial problems. Complexity of computer computations. Springer, Boston, MA, 1972. 85-103.
instanceFormat: Format: {(U,S,K) | U is set, S subset {a | a subset U}} Example: ({1,2,3,4,5},{{1,2,3},{2,4},{3,4},{4,5}},3)
certificateFormat: Format: {sub1,...,subK} subset S | union of chosen subsets covers the universal set U Example: {{1,2,3},{4,5}}

defaultSolver.solverDefinition: This is a brute force solver for the NP-Complete Set Cover problem
